summary: A work only counts as evidence for a two-sided claim when its abstract or title names BOTH the intervention and the outcome — but ANY token of a side may carry that side, because the literature swaps a claim's modifiers while keeping its head noun.
reason: The lexical relevance gate keeps any work sharing a single content token with the claim, so a vaccine-schedule paper that never mentions autism entered the corpus and helped carry a false 'supports' verdict. Requiring both claim sides is the cheapest filter that cannot be satisfied by half a topic, and it must hold on keyless runs where no LLM vets relevance. Matching a side on its first token alone is what a regen must not go back to: a corpus measurement showed 'artificial sweeteners' reduced to 'artif' dropped 69% of the sweetener corpus including the on-point meta-analyses, which write 'low-calorie sweeteners'. An unsplittable claim yields empty token lists and bypasses the gate rather than filtering blind.
validated_outcome: go build/vet clean, full go test suite green including new TestIsPICORelevant and TestPICOTokens; relevant_count now reports the post-PICO corpus and a zero-survivor run emits an insufficient result instead of a verdict computed from nothing.
